In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of amino acid replacements that cause temperature‐sensitive growth of E. coli K12 and that are located in aminoacyl‐ tRNA synthetases.

the identification of a single amino acid change in the Escherichiacoli asnS40 gene which is responsible for an increase in the K m values for ATP and asparagine in the ATP‐PP i exchange and aminoacylation reaction.
the identification of a temperature‐sensitive mutant of asparaginly‐tRNA synthase (Asn‐RS) and with the characterization of the mutated enzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the replacement of Pro‐231 by Leu in motif 2 of Escherichia colli AsnRS leads to a large increase in the K m values for ATP and asparagine in the ATP‐PP i and aminoacylation reactions.
motif 2 in the asparaginase‐tRNA synthase is involved in the binding of the amino acid and the adenine moiety of the ATP molecule.
the replacement of Pro‐231 by a Leu residue in AsnRS causes a significant increase in K m values for both substrates in the aminoacylation and the ATP‐PP i exchange reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P231L mutant enzyme is defective in aminoacylation, probably due to a decreased ability of the enzyme to bind asparagine and to activate asparagine to the aminoacyl‐adenylate.
the P231L mutant enzyme has a significantly increased K m value (for ATP and asparagine) in the ATP‐PP i exchange reaction and the aminoacylation activity, but the V max value is not changed.
Pro‐231 is essential for the correct function of the Escherichi a coli AsnRS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proline residue at this position is essential for amino acid activation by class II aminoacyltRNA synthetases.
the amino acid replacement P231L is responsible for the temperature‐sensitivity of the mutant strain.
the amino acid replacement in motif 3 of the AsnRS is not responsible for the observed temperature sensitivity of the HO202 mutant strain.
